headline: Braga sack their coach two days before unbeaten Gent
summary: Braga host Gent in the Conference League two days after sacking head coach Carlos Vicens, and Franclim Carvalho takes charge. He inherits one win in five and a defence that conceded eight goals in those games, according to Goal.com; Braga's Conference League opener ended 0-3 at Copenhagen. Gent arrive unbeaten and made 2.24 expected goals in their opener. Even so, the market average keeps Braga favourites: their win chance slipped from 56.5% to 51.3%, the handicap line is 0.56 in their favour, and the goals line is 2.25.
read: Braga are still favourites at home, but their fair win chance has slipped from 56.5% to 51.3% and the handicap has come back from -0.78 to -0.56, with Gent unbeaten in five and Braga on three defeats in that same span. The backdrop is a coaching change two days out: Carlos Vicens out, Franclim Carvalho in, against a Gent team whose only setback this season was a 3-3 cup draw at Rochefort. The goals market sits at 2.25, split almost exactly down the middle.

facts.fact: Braga sacked head coach Carlos Vicens and appointed Franclim Carvalho two days before this match.
facts.meaning: A brand-new manager takes his first game with almost no time on the training ground, so nobody knows quite what Braga will look like.

facts.fact: Braga's fair win chance fell from 56.5% to 51.3% in the 24 hours before kick-off.
facts.meaning: Braga are still the favourites, but the gap to Gent has narrowed noticeably.

facts.fact: Braga's last five results read LLLDW, with a 1-0 win over Estoril the only victory.
facts.meaning: The team the new coach inherits is short of wins and short of goals, not just short of a manager.

facts.fact: Braga have conceded eight goals across their last five matches, according to Goal.com.
facts.meaning: A defence leaking almost two goals a game is a serious problem against a Gent side that has scored nine in five.

facts.fact: Braga lost their Conference League opener 0-3 at Copenhagen and sit 35th of 36 in the league table.
facts.meaning: They are already playing catch-up in the competition, with a goal difference of -3 after one game.

facts.fact: Gent are unbeaten in their last five: DWWWD, three wins and two draws.
facts.meaning: Rik De Mil's side travel to Portugal in the best form of the two teams.

facts.fact: Gent beat Aarhus 1-0 in their Conference League opener with 2.24 xG to 0.23 against.
facts.meaning: The scoreline flattered Aarhus — Gent created the chances of a much bigger win and sit 13th of 36.

facts.fact: Gent were knocked out of the Belgian Cup at Rochefort after a 3-3 draw, their only blemish of the season.
facts.meaning: Their unbeaten run in normal time survived it, but the extra workload is why they played four days ago.

sources.fact: SC Braga sacked head coach Carlos Vicens with immediate effect following a disappointing spell.
Franclim Carvalho was officially appointed as Braga's new head coach, succeeding Carlos Vicens.
Braga president Salvador described the coaching swap as a cut rather than a transition.
Carlos Vicens departed after Braga's home defeat to Gil Vicente.
New coach Franclim Carvalho said he had always wanted to sit in the Braga dugout.
Braga have conceded eight goals across their last five matches, with a 1-0 win over Estoril the only bright spot, per Goal.com.
Gent coach Rik De Mil has an almost fully available squad for the trip to Braga, though a few names are missing and one defender returns to the selection.
Gent were unbeaten this season until a cup defeat to Union Rochefortoise knocked them out of the Belgian Cup round of 16.
